predecessors.text: the left bank of the Dniester, then part of the Moldavian SSR, which the 2 September 1990 congress proclaimed a separate republic; six 15 km circles on the river intersected with Moldova, 14 grid…

ledger.x: 2 September 1990: Transnistria proclaims itself a separate republic.
5 November 1991: the republic drops its Soviet label.
21 July 1992: Yeltsin and Snegur sign the ceasefire.

wars.name: Transnistria War
wars.outcome: Transnistria became de facto independent but remained internationally recognised as part of Moldova; ceasefire of 21 July 1992 with a Joint Control Commission and a mixed peacekeeping force; nearly 1,000 dead.

certainty.note: Boundary of the proclaimed republic undefined on the pages.
A ceasefire line, not a recognised border; Moldova's special status law of 22 July 2005 excludes Bender and the Moldovan-held areas; the pages give no coordinates.
